body.statement: Consider the linear Gaussian perfect-intervention subclass satisfying the common non-margin hypotheses of Acartürk et al.'s graph theorem and the observed-conditioning bound \(\kappa\). Section 5 of that source selects \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\), where equation (22) defines the all-subset positive-eigenvalue minimum, and independently selects \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), where printed equation (23) defines \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\min_i\|H_{i,:}\|_2\|G_{:,i}\|_2\). Fix \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=g_0/2\) and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=h_0/2\). On the common actual-geometry subregion satisfying the reached projector band \(c_{t,j}(P)\in\{0\}\cup[h_0,1]\), the complete fixed-margin source premise \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\ge g_0\), \(\eta_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\eta^{\ast}(P))\), and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}\in(0,\gamma^{\ast}(G))\), together with strictly positive continuously differentiable support-coordinate densities and causal conditionals, one distinct single-target intervention per node, Assumption 1's parent-ratio condition, and score-difference consistency (15), implies the two transcript-local bands: equation (22) bounds every reached positive eigenvalue below by \(g_0\), and the common actual-geometry restriction supplies the reached projector band. Proposition 1 separately certifies that each nonzero comparison witnessed by label \(i\) is at least \(\rho_i(G)\). Therefore this fixed-margin source region restricted by the common reached projector band is contained in \(\mathcal P_{\mathsf A}(g_0,h_0,\kappa)\). The inclusion is strict at \((g_0,h_0,\kappa)=(1/40,1/2,32)\) for every \(n\ge4\): \(\mathfrak F_n\) satisfies all listed non-margin source conditions, every reached comparison is zero or one, \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)=\rho^{\ast}(G)=1\), and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{src}}=1/4\in(0,1)\), but it lies outside the source region because \(\eta^{\ast}(P)\le2^{-2n-1}<\eta_{\mathrm{src}}=1/80\), while Theorem 1 certifies it from the reached bands. No containment of the uncorrected published premise in the transcript-local class is asserted, because a lower bound on the printed norm product \(\gamma^{\ast}(G)\) does not imply a lower bound on the reciprocal projector scale \(\rho^{\ast}(G)\) or on the actual comparisons.
body.justification: The theorem isolates the strict relaxation of the source's all-subset spectral premise while keeping its printed threshold condition and the actual projector geometry distinct.
body.gap: Acartürk et al.'s Lemma 13 controls ranks for every subset through the global minimum; no checked source proves that the executed program admits a strictly larger constant-gap class.
body.consumer: Users can certify easy executions that fail the source's global rank-threshold premise while exposing the separate actual projector gap used by the implementation.
